ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances and is over the 1.0 km tolerance. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 14.6 km against optimal_distance_km of 12.7 km, a deviation of 1.90 km, and the deviation_pct is recorded as 15.0. That is 0.90 km beyond POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the trip travelled materially further than the recommended route and the excess is not within tolerance.

The route actually taken is confirmed by the driver-device trace and the trip event log, and it is not the recommended route. The recommended route ran via Clementi Avenue 2, Ayer Rajah Expressway (AYE), Keppel Road and Wallich Street (12.7 km), while the vehicle left the recommended route at the AYE / West Coast Highway exit at 18:05:06 and did not rejoin until Keppel Road / Telok Blangah Road at 18:20:12 - roughly fifteen minutes off the recommended route, over West Coast Highway and Pasir Panjang Road, in a trip that was itself only 26 minutes long. Under POL-RD-22 the trace shows which route was taken and when; the recorded platform distances, not the sparse trace, measure the deviation.

There is no traffic data justifying a reroute of the recommended route. The LTA record for the recommended carriageway - Ayer Rajah Expressway (AYE) towards City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct - for a window (17:29:34 to 18:59:34 on 18/8/2026) that brackets the entire trip is advisory_type NONE, and it states in terms that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded there and that speed bands were 4-6 throughout. A NONE advisory is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident), so the driver's assertion of an 'AYE jam' is contradicted by the traffic data for the very segment he was supposed to use, and the rider's own statement that the AYE looked clear when they passed the slip road is consistent with that data.

The only non-NONE advisory in the record does not supply the missing justification. EV-ADVIS-05006-02 is a ROADWORK with Lane 1 closed on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah, near Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre. POL-RD-23 requires an advisory that intersects the RECOMMENDED route, and the recommended route for this trip ran via Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road and Wallich Street - Pasir Panjang Road is not one of those roads; it is a road the deviating route used. The artifact does not itself assert a justification: its justifies_reroute and intersects_route fields are both null, and the record expressly leaves the question to the Judge. A field the evidence leaves undetermined is not a 'yes', and the rider should not carry the disputed charge on an unresolved field.

The rider's acknowledgment, whatever weight it is given, does not save the driver's position. Even on the driver's most favourable reading - that his 18:01:46 message 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' and the rider's 'ok' at 18:02:11 constituted notice and agreement under POL-RD-21, notice having preceded the 18:05:06 deviation - row (a) of the refund matrix still requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and it is not. The case therefore falls in row (d), not row (a): 'not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare in full'. Row (d) turns on justification alone and pays the whole excess distance fare; the driver cannot convert a non-justified detour into a no-refund case by pointing at a chat message.

The sum the driver seeks to claw back is exactly the sum POL-RD-24(d) requires to be refunded, and it has already been refunded. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance at the base per-km rate without surge: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.368, rounded half-up to 1.37 SGD, which is precisely the figure the fare breakdown carries as refund_issued_sgd (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) and the figure the platform moved by the fare_adjusted event of 2026-08-19T01:56:34+08:00. The rider is already in the position the policy prescribes; the driver's claim asks to restore a charge the policy says must not stand. The driver filed this dispute, so the outcome that leaves the refund intact is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands.

No fact this case needs is missing, so the escalation route in POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. Both recorded distances are present in the trip record, the fares reconcile to the ledger, the chat log is contiguous and matches the recorded chat_message_count of 4, and the traffic advisories were retrieved by the platform for the queried segment and window. Every artifact in the package is COMPLETE with a weight_multiplier of 1.0. There is no open question for a human reviewer to answer, and escalating would hold a sum the arithmetic already settles.

The AI may issue this ruling finally rather than escalate. The deviation is 1.90 km, within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km limit, and the contested value is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final line. Neither profile carries a fraud_flags value of 1 or more, so the ordinary confidence threshold of 0.80 applies and no elevated 0.95 threshold is triggered. By contrast with a case such as a 4.3 km deviation, nothing here puts the decision out of the AI's hands.

Notice was given before the point of deviation and the rider agreed to it: MSG-05006-003 (driver, sent 18:01:46) asked 'Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?', the rider read it at 18:02:06 and answered 'ok' at 18:02:11 (MSG-05006-004, read 18:02:35), and the platform's own event record puts the vehicle's departure from the recommended route at the AYE / West Coast Highway exit at 18:05:06 — three minutes after the acknowledgment. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and here the chat log does exactly that, on complete artifacts carrying weight 1.0.

The rider's acknowledgment is unrebutted: her counterparty statement objects only that 'the longer road cost more' and never denies that she answered 'ok' to the West Coast Highway proposal, so on POL-RD-21 the deviation was an agreed route choice, not a unilateral detour visited on her. On the platform's recorded distances the deviation is 1.90 km (14.6 minus 12.7, per POL-RD-22's recorded-distance measure), over the 1 km tolerance, which puts the case in POL-RD-24(a) — informed and agreed, over 1 km — rather than the 'not informed' row (b). A row that returns nothing to the rider leaves the 1.37 SGD already recovered from the driver's earnings to be restored to him as DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-GEN-03.

The remedy the driver asks for is the exact figure the platform has already moved: fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd 1.37 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings by the fare_adjusted event at 2026-08-19T01:56:34+08:00. The contested amount is 1.37 SGD — below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so no confidence floor and no value-based escalation applies — and the deviation of 1.90 km is inside POL-RD-25's 2 km limb, so the AI may rule this case on its merits now rather than defer it, and the DRIVER_COMPENSATION figure under POL-GEN-03 is 1.37 SGD.

In the alternative, if the traffic limb of POL-RD-23 is not accepted on this record, the case should go to a human rather than be closed against the driver. The AYE advisory (EV-ADVIS-05006-01) returns type NONE, so it records neither incident nor closure and its type is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names, while the trip-window closure-kind advisory (EV-ADVIS-05006-02), a ROADWORK valid 09:00–23:00 on 18/8, has an intersection with the route that the same derived block expressly leaves undetermined; against the driver's contemporaneous in-app report of the jam, that limb is not cleanly negated, and where a fact POL-RD-23 needs cannot be established the case is escalated under POL-GEN-26 with the 1.37 SGD held rather than confirmed against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Driver — the route you took ran 1.90 km further than the recommended route (recorded actual 14.6 km against recommended 12.7 km, POL-RD-22's recorded-distance measure), past the 1.0 km tolerance. What the refund turns on under POL-RD-24 is whether the reroute was traffic-justified, not whether the rider agreed. POL-RD-23 requires traffic data for the recommended AYE segment itself showing congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA record for the AYE towards the City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01), is type NONE and reports no incident, roadwork or closure with speed bands 4-6 across the trip window; the only non-NONE record (EV-ADVIS-05006-02) is a roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah, and Pasir Panjang Road is not on the recommended route (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street), so it does not intersect the route POL-RD-23 asks about. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified, and row (d) applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full — 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.37 SGD. Rider — that 1.37 SGD is exactly the sum already refunded to you and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.37, payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, the fare_adjusted event of 2026-08-19T01:56:34+08:00), so the present state already matches the policy and it stands. On the chat: the driver's 18:01:46 message and your 'ok' at 18:02:11 do establish notice before the deviation the platform logged at 18:05:06, and I accept that under POL-RD-21; but row (a) of POL-RD-24 also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, which it is not, so the agreement does not move the case to the no-refund row. On escalation: the driver's fallback that the roadwork advisory's route-intersection is 'undetermined' does not open POL-GEN-26 — that question is decided from the advisory's own road, direction and location, and Pasir Panjang Road is not on the recommended route, so the limb is cleanly negated and no fact the rules need is missing or impaired (every artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0). Who decides: the contested value is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final line, and the deviation of 1.90 km is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit, so this ruling issues finally. The outcome is read against you, the driver, who filed: your claim to have the 1.37 SGD restored is not supported and the present state stands, so the ruling is NO_ACTION with both amounts null.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
